info.title: PredMart API
info.description: API for PredMart decentralized lending platform

get.description: Generate a one-time nonce for SIWE signing.

post.description: Verify SIWE signature, auto-register user, issue JWT.

get.description:
Get EIP-712 typed data for signing a borrow intent.

`recipient` is the destination address for the borrowed USDC.e — frontend
always passes the user's Safe so funds land on Safe (V2-native default).

post.description:
Submit a signed borrow intent via the relayer.

The backend fetches a fresh oracle price at this moment (never exposed
to the user), then submits both signatures in a single transaction.
Waits for on-chain receipt before returning.

get.description: Pool-level statistics. Fast path uses DB snapshot + 1 RPC.
Per-wallet interest correction for donation artifacts.

Get a specific borrower position with optional risk metrics.

Pass ?price=<WAD> to get health_factor, ltv, and liquidation_threshold.
Get all positions for a user (active, enriched with on-chain debt).
Get lending event history for a user, optionally filtered by token_id and/or event_type.

Historical pool rate snapshots for Supply APY / Borrow APR charts.
Real APY from pUSDC exchange rate growth (accounts for bad debt).

Depth gate status for UI indicators. Returns full/limited/blocked per token.

Fast path: read pre-warmed entries from ``eligibility:current`` (HOT tier
refreshes short_duration tokens every 300s, COLD tier handles the rest
every 5 min). One batched HMGET → sub-ms response.

Fallback path: per-token live compute via ``get_depth_status``. Triggers
only on cache miss — typically newly-tracked tokens between HOT cycles or
one-off lookups for tokens outside the tracked set. On-demand results are
written back to the cache hash (self-warming), guarded by a short SETNX
lock to avoid stampede on concurrent requests for the same token.

Read-only oracle price for the leverage UI's LTV bound. Returns the same
per-share price the contract's LTV check would use right now, so the UI's
``simulateLeverage`` math matches what ``leverageDeposit`` will accept
on-chain.

Lazy cache with stampede protection:
  - Cache hit → sub-ms Redis read.
  - Cache miss → SETNX lock on a sibling key. Lock holder computes,
    writes ``ORACLE_PRICE_CACHE_PREFIX{tid}`` with TTL, releases lock.
    Concurrent waiters poll the cache for ~600ms; if it lands they
    return the freshly-cached value, otherwise they fall back to
    computing themselves (the lock holder may have crashed).

The lock keeps recompute rate at one per-market per-TTL even when many
users are polling concurrently — without it, every cache expiry would
fan out into N parallel depth walks, scaling linearly with users.

Batched read of several tokens' oracle (Mark) prices in ONE request.

The leverage panel prefetches BOTH outcomes of a binary market and keeps
them in memory, so toggling YES/NO swaps to an already-cached price with no
fetch round-trip. Without it the panel briefly valued the newly-selected
side's position against the *other* side's stale Mark, flashing a
nonsensical Health Factor for ~500ms on every toggle.

Per-token failures (thin book, etc.) return a null price plus a structured
``errors[tid]`` entry instead of failing the whole batch, so one illiquid
side never blanks the other. Each token reuses the same Redis cache + lock
as ``/oracle-price/{id}`` via the shared ``_resolve_oracle_price`` helper.

Ask-side orderbook + depth buffer for the leverage UI's
`simulateLeverage` math. Returned `asks` and `buffer_bps` mirror exactly
what `leverage_open_engine.execute_leverage_open` walks against in its
pre-flight `pessimistic_fill` check, so the frontend's "max leverage"
matches what the backend will actually accept.

The frontend polls this every ~3s (mirroring `useOraclePrice`) and walks
the asks locally for whatever USDC size the slider currently shows —
slider drag stays sub-ms, no per-step API call. Backend caching lives in
`get_live_book` (WS state ≤10s old, REST fallback 5s TTL), so even at
10k users this endpoint hits Polymarket at most once per token per ~5s.
Contract addresses, chain info, and protocol parameters for frontend.

Single-call leverage-open prepare. Computes the advance amount, builds
the outer wallet-bundle the user signs, persists prep state, and returns
the bundle's EIP-712 typed-data + a leverage_id. The user signs the
bundle in MetaMask, then POSTs {leverage_id, signature} to
/leverage/open to broadcast.

State-creating GET — emits Cache-Control: no-store so intermediaries
don't cache the leverage_id between requests.

post.description:
Submit the user-signed outer bundle. Backend relays the bundle via
Polymarket (SAFE-type for Safes, WALLET-type for DepositWallets) and
starts the background task that completes the CLOB buy + leverageDeposit.

All other parameters (auth tuple, user_amount, advance_amount, bundle
bytes) were locked in by /leverage/auth-data and live in the prep cache.
The frontend supplies only the leverage_id + signature so it can't smuggle
different parameters between sign-time and broadcast-time.

Ensure user exists for a wallet address. Creates if not exists.
Called by frontend when wallet connects (before SIWE auth).
Fetches Polymarket profile on first creation.

put.description:
Update user profile. Only the wallet owner can update.
- username: Optional new username (1-30 chars, alphanumeric + underscores)

These are local overrides — Polymarket profile data is used as fallback.

get.description:
Profile activity feed — leverage trading only.

Returns PredMart leverage opens + closes. Polymarket-spot trades and
lender vault flows are intentionally excluded; users see those on
polymarket.com and the lending dashboard respectively.

Download an Excel file explaining why a liquidation occurred.

The file shows the best bid (the Mark) and best ask over time against the
position's liquidation-threshold price: the position is liquidated once the
best bid falls to/below that threshold (health factor < 1).

Get portfolio summary for a wallet address.
Resolves Polymarket proxy wallet, fetches positions + USDC.e balance.

List market groups. Serves from a Redis-cached pre-computed response
on the no-filter hot path; falls through to in-process compute against
_store when filtered. Response is enriched with per-sub-market eligibility;
groups with no leverageable sub-market are filtered out.
Return curated header categories (broad topics).
Return trending tags computed from active events.
Search events/groups by title and tags. Returns matching tag suggestions + events.
Resolve a slug to either a market or group.
Get a single market by slug or condition_id.

List sibling events in a recurring series (e.g. hourly BTC Up/Down).

Returns events sorted by end_date ascending (candle order). Each item exposes:
  - slug + title for navigation
  - start_date / end_date (UTC, ISO)
  - state: "past" | "live" | "future" derived from end_date vs now
    (Gamma's `closed` flag lags actual market end by hours, so we compute)
  - last_yes_price + winning_side (winning_side detected from outcome
    prices >= 0.95, regardless of Gamma's closed flag)
Get a single group by slug.
Get price history for a market from Polymarket CLOB.

Get aggregated orderbook for a market side (YES/NO) from Polymarket CLOB.

For neg_risk markets, the raw CLOB book for a token shows asks at ~0.999
(literal sell orders). Polymarket derives "implied" asks from the complementary
token's bids: if NO bids at 0.997, that implies YES asks at 1 - 0.997 = 0.003.
This endpoint performs that transformation for neg_risk markets.
Get user's position in a specific market from Polymarket data-api.

Return EIP-712 typed data for ClobAuth signature.

The frontend signs this with MetaMask, then calls Polymarket CLOB
/auth/derive-api-key directly to get L2 keys. Keys stay in the browser.

Return EIP-712 typed data for Gnosis Safe proxy creation.

If the user already has a deployed Safe, returns {already_deployed: true}.
Otherwise, returns the typed data for the user to sign with MetaMask.

post.description:
Submit proxy deployment via Polymarket relayer (gasless for user).

Takes the user's EIP-712 SafeProxy signature and submits to the relayer.
The relayer sends the TX on-chain and pays gas. Frontend polls /relay-status.

Wrapped in try/except so relayer-side errors surface as 4xx with CORS
headers attached (an unhandled 500 strips CORS and the browser shows
`Failed to fetch` instead of the real cause).

Confirm Safe deployment after user sent the TX from their wallet.

Verifies the proxy exists on-chain and saves it to the DB.
Called by the frontend after the createProxy TX is confirmed.

get.description:
Poll the status of a relayed transaction.

Returns the relayer state (STATE_NEW, STATE_MINED, STATE_CONFIRMED, STATE_FAILED).
When STATE_MINED or STATE_CONFIRMED, the frontend can proceed to the next step.
If wallet is provided and the TX is a deploy, also saves proxy_wallet to DB.

Check which trading setup steps are complete for a wallet.

Returns:
  - safe_deployed:   true iff a Polymarket wallet of any supported type
                     exists on-chain at `proxy_wallet`. Name kept for
                     frontend backward-compat; semantically means
                     "Step 1 done" for both Safe and DepositWallet users.
  - proxy_wallet:    the wallet address (Safe or DepositWallet), or null
  - wallet_type:     "gnosis_safe" | "deposit_wallet" | "none" — frontend
                     uses this to pick the right signing path in Step 3
  - approvals:       token approval status (or null if no wallet)

CLOB key status is checked client-side (keys live in localStorage).

Return typed-data the user signs to approve all PredMart-required token
allowances. Branches on wallet type:

  - Gnosis Safe path  → SafeTx (MultiSend, operation=1). Frontend signs
                        via `personal_sign` of the SafeTx hash; backend
                        submits as `SAFE`-type to Polymarket's relayer.
  - DepositWallet path → DepositWallet `Batch`. Frontend signs via
                        `signTypedData` (EIP-712 structured). Backend
                        submits as `WALLET`-type. No module-enable step
                        (DWs have no module system).

The response always includes `signing_method` and `wallet_type` so the
frontend can pick the right signer without re-detecting on its own.

post.description:
Submit token approvals via Polymarket relayer (gasless for user).

Branches on wallet type: Safe → execTransaction (SAFE-type relayer);
DepositWallet → WALLET-batch. Polymarket's relayer pays gas in both cases.

Any exception is converted to a 400 with a clear detail so the Starlette
CORS middleware attaches `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and the browser
surfaces the real error instead of `Failed to fetch`.

get.description:
Return EIP-712 SafeTx data for lending pool approvals.

User signs and sends execTransaction directly (pays gas).
Separate from Polymarket approvals which go through their relayer.

post.description:
Build execTransaction calldata for lending pool approval.

User sends this as a raw TX via MetaMask (pays gas).

get.description:
Return the typed-data the user signs for a gasless withdraw. Dispatches
by wallet type: Safe path returns a SafeTx (+ safe_tx_hash for
personal_sign); DepositWallet path returns an EIP-712 Batch for
signTypedData. The `signing_method` field tells the frontend which
branch to take (same contract as the leverage-open prep endpoint).

post.description:
Submit withdraw via Polymarket relayer. Dispatches by wallet type to
SAFE relayer (Safe path) or WALLET relayer (DepositWallet path).

get.description:
Return the typed-data the user signs for a gasless repay. Dispatches
by wallet type: Safe path returns a SafeTx (+ safe_tx_hash for
personal_sign); DepositWallet path returns an EIP-712 Batch for
signTypedData. The `signing_method` field tells the frontend which
branch to take.

post.description:
Submit repay via Polymarket relayer. Dispatches by wallet type:
DW echo fields present → WALLET relayer; else → SAFE relayer.

get.description:
Return SafeTx hash for personal_sign — gasless deposit collateral via Polymarket relayer.

Backend signs an oracle PriceData (skip_depth_gate=True since this is not a
borrow) and bakes it into the depositCollateral calldata. PriceData has a
60s on-chain TTL — ample for normal sign + relay submission round-trip.

post.description:
Submit Safe-signed depositCollateral via Polymarket relayer (gasless for user).

The frontend echoes back the exact (to, data, operation, nonce) returned by
/deposit-collateral-relayer-data — necessary because the embedded oracle
PriceData is non-deterministic. The on-chain Safe verifies the signature
against the submitted bytes; bad echo just fails verification harmlessly.

get.description:
Return CLOB market info (fees, tick size, order status).

Frontend uses this to display Polymarket fee rates and validate orders.

Return all users with aggregated lending, login, and liquidation data.

Uses a CTE to union wallets from all sources (users table, lending_events,

Return high-level platform summary stats.

of pool assets each token represents.

Uses Redis cache for debt data (updated every 5s by position tracker).
Falls back to on-chain reads only if cache is empty.

Enhanced pool health metrics for admin dashboard.

Cached for 15s to avoid 13 on-chain RPC reads on every poll.
The 30s polling interval means at most 2 polls hit cache, 1 refreshes.

Raw event log across all users — most recent first.

Acknowledge bad_debt_absorbed or advance_expired events.

Writes acknowledged_at into the params JSONB. Dashboard queries

get.description:
Alert banner data for the admin dashboard.

Returns a compact summary of things that need immediate attention:
indexer health, pending advances, stuck operations, today's P&L,
and critical reconciliation failures. Designed so the admin can
glance at it in 3 seconds and know if everything is OK or not.

Rolling ~15-min VM resource window populated by `lending.tasks.snapshot_vm_metrics` (every 2 min).
Window is oldest-first for direct chart consumption; `latest` mirrors the newest entry.
Frontend computes the headline numbers as a mean across the window (a 15-min rolling average
that tracks GCP-style smoothed metrics rather than a single momentary sample).

Recent InfrastructureEvent rows for daily admin review.

Returns events from the last `hours` hours (default 24, max 168=7d). The
`critical` flag mirrors the health endpoint's whitelist so the dashboard
can distinguish wake-at-3am events from dashboard-only noise.
By default acknowledged events are hidden; pass include_acknowledged=true
to see the full history.

List whitelisted markets with diagnostic stats per row.

Returns active entries by default; pass include_removed=true to also see
audit history (soft-deleted rows).

post.description: Add a market to the lending whitelist (idempotent).
Soft-remove a market from the whitelist (audit history preserved).

get.description:
Return typed-data for a 1-call WALLET batch: onramp.wrap(USDC.e, dw, amount).

Response includes the full EIP-712 envelope ready for
`eth_signTypedData_v4` (EIP712Domain types injected so a raw JSON-RPC
sign call can use it without extra prep), plus the calls/nonce/deadline
the caller passes back to the submit endpoint.

post.description:
Submit the signed 1-call WALLET batch to Polymarket. Returns the raw
relayer response on success, or the verbatim error body on failure — so
we can see exactly what Polymarket says.

get.description:
Return the full league catalog. Frontend uses this to build the sports
sidebar and to filter events by series_slug / tag.

Response shape:
  {
    "leagues": { "<url_slug>": { "kind": "series"|"tag", ... } },
    "umbrella_slugs": [...],
    "generated_at_ms": int,
    "url_slug_count": int,
    "resolved_count": int,
    "unresolved": [...]
  }

post.description:
Force-refresh the catalog. Admin-gated because each call triggers a
~5s upstream scrape (Polymarket /sports + /tags pagination + landing
page). Unauthenticated, it would be a low-cost DoS vector and could
trip Polymarket rate-limits on the backend's egress IP.

get.description: Crawler-facing OG page. Humans are redirected to the winner's profile.
The share card itself, composited server-side from the position record.

Start the Discord link. Requires a PredMart session (SIWE-issued JWT) so
we know which wallet to credit. Returns {authorize_url} for the frontend to
navigate to.

OAuth redirect target. No JWT here — the trusted wallet identity comes from
the Redis `state` minted at /oauth/login; the state cookie additionally binds
the flow to the browser that started it (login-CSRF guard).

Auth-gated readiness probe. Returns 200/503 with the build version and
the NAMES of any failed checks — no exception strings, no internal
hostnames, no library versions. Exception details for each failed check
are LOGGED at WARNING so operators can read them in container logs.

Three structural checks (Redis, Postgres, markets store) fail-fast when
the platform is genuinely unable to serve users. A fourth check surfaces
the runtime CRITICAL signal from `get_health()` — so BetterStack catches
the conditions that genuinely warrant operator intervention
(stuck liquidations, RPC pool down, oracle insane, relayer gas critical,
indexer way behind, writer dead, unacknowledged critical
infra events). `get_health()` has internal anti-flap (startup grace,
sustained-condition gates) so a single-tick transient doesn't 503.
Returns {debug: true} if the request comes from an allowed debug IP.
